title: When Prompting Fails to Sway: Inertia in Moral and Value Judgments of Large Language Models
religious_groups: Do not belong to a denomination
findings: The study found that LLMs exhibit a strong 'inertia' in their moral and value judgments. Assigning a persona with a specific religious belief, as part of a broader set of demographic attributes, did not significantly sway the models' underlying value orientations. Models consistently maintained default stances, particularly on harm avoidance and fairness, regardless of the religious (or other demographic) cues provided in the prompt.
references: Marwa Abdulhai, Gregory Serapio-Garcia, Clément Crepy, Daria Valter, John Canny, and Natasha Jaques. 2023. Moral foundations of large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.15337.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the influence of religious identity (as part of a randomized demographic persona) on the stability of Large Language Models' responses to moral and value-based questionnaires (MFQ-30 and PVQ-RR).
